note: Meets every stated criterion, and meets the 'physician' example literally — the ICP quote names physicians and he is one, with a master's and PhD in physiology on top. Income is evidenced rather than assumed ('I made too much, so I had to pay a lot' in tax); the constraint is cash-flow timing, not capacity. Strength training is the precisely neglected corner of an otherwise fit life — VO2 max 52, eight marathons, and 'true strength training, which I've ignored for most of my adult life'. And he is explicitly good-to-great: 'I'm not fat, my arms are muscular, my legs are muscular', wanting recomposition rather than rescue. The finding here is not the fit but what the fit conceals: a textbook core-ICP prospect walked in with a displaced scapula and surgery booked for November, and the stated ICP has no clinical criterion that would surface that at any point in the qualification.
